summary: Changes the IANA registration procedure for the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry, which RFC 5029 created, from Standards Action to Expert Review. This makes it easier to allocate new bit values. It updates RFC 5029.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9650 changes the approval process for new values in the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry. Requests now use Expert Review instead of Standards Action.

subtitle: Changes the registration procedure for IS-IS neighbor link-attribute bits.

tldr.problem: The IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry used Standards Action, which the RFC says was unnecessarily restrictive and increased the risk of unregistered code point use.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the registry procedure to Expert Review and adds this document as a registry reference.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9650 updates RFC 5029; the security issues discussed in RFC 5029 are unchanged.

today: RFC 9650 is a Proposed Standard from August 2024 and updates RFC 5029.

sections.title: The Existing Registration Procedure
sections.content:
RFC 5029 established the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry and set its registration procedure to Standards Action. RFC 9650 says this was unnecessarily restrictive because it prevented allocation of bits to experimental protocols.

The RFC also identifies a risk that an overly restrictive process could encourage use of unregistered code points, known as code point squatting.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier rules required a Standards Action to assign a bit. The RFC says this made experimental assignments difficult and could encourage people to use unregistered values.

sections.title: Expert Review Replaces Standards Action
sections.content:
IANA changed the registration procedure for the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry to Expert Review, as described by RFC 8126. IANA also listed RFC 9650 as a reference for the registry.

General guidance for the designated experts is in RFC 7370, with more specific guidance in RFC 5029.
sections.plainLanguage: New registry requests now go through Expert Review. The designated experts use general guidance from RFC 7370 and specific guidance from RFC 5029.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that this change does not affect the security issues discussed in RFC 5029. It revises only the registration procedure for the IS-IS Neighbor Link-Attribute Bit Values registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration change does not alter the security issues described in RFC 5029.
